name: Aedon.Charities
shortDescription: A UK Salesforce-native charity accounting platform for SORP reporting, fund and project accounting, partial VAT, Gift Aid submissions and donor tax statements.
suitableContexts: Church charities with complex fund, project, donor or multi-entity finance needs
Finance teams that use or intend to use Salesforce
Charities with annual turnover above the supplier's stated £500,000 focus

pricing.summary: Aedon publishes £145 per month for a full Aedon.Charities user and £40 per month for a reviewer, plus £50 per additional company. The page says ten Salesforce Cloud licences are included and annual or longer commitments can reduce price. The supplier also states a one-year minimum subscription; obtain VAT treatment, implementation, migration, Salesforce configuration, payment, integration and termination costs in writing.

startingPrice.qualifier: published full-user price, before VAT if applicable

tiers.detail: Supplier's published per-full-user charity accounting price.

tiers.label: Additional company
tiers.detail: Published per-additional-company price; the package states three companies are included.

gdprInformation: Aedon.Co publishes a privacy policy for its website and says some personal data may be stored in the UK and India. That policy is not a product data-processing agreement. Because Aedon.Charities is Salesforce-native and handles charity financial and donor-related data, a church should obtain the product DPA, controller-processor allocation, Salesforce and Aedon sub-processor list, hosting and transfer safeguards, retention, role permissions, audit logging, backup, breach process and complete export arrangements before implementation.
integrations: SmarterPay Direct Debits and bulk payments described as optional
Confirm the current implementation, licence and integration scope
importExport: Supplier describes accounting, reporting and payment-file workflows within Salesforce
Request migration templates and full finance, fund, donor, Gift Aid, audit-trail, attachment and configuration export documentation
support: Supplier lists Aedon.Academy, phone and Microsoft Teams support, remote support and an annual health check
Supplier describes implementation as typically within one VAT quarter
Confirm included implementation, support hours, response commitments and training scope

uk-operator.value: Companies House records AEDON.CO LIMITED (14278135) as an active English private limited company, and the supplier privacy policy identifies it as the site operator.

charity-scope.value: Supplier describes Aedon.Charities as a specialist accounting platform for UK charities with turnover above £500,000, including SORP, fund, project, VAT, Gift Aid and donor-tax-statement functions.

pricing-and-support.value: Supplier publishes full-user, reviewer and additional-company prices, included Salesforce Cloud licences, package functions and support materials.

data-location-boundary.value: The supplier's website privacy policy states that some personal data may be stored in the UK and India; it does not establish the product data-processing arrangement.

editorial.assessment: Aedon.Charities is a UK charity-accounting product built inside Salesforce, rather than a conventional church finance package or a general church-management system. Its stated SORP, fund, project, VAT, Gift Aid and donor-tax capability could suit a larger church charity already committed to Salesforce. Its published entry price, implementation shape and Salesforce operating model are likely excessive for most small congregations, so it belongs in a narrow enterprise-style accounting shortlist rather than as a default recommendation.
bestFor: Larger church charities with complex restricted funds, projects or multiple legal entities
Finance teams wanting their accounting and Salesforce charity data in one platform
Organisations with budget and capability for a structured Salesforce implementation
strengths: Published charity-specific price and functional scope
Explicit SORP, fund accounting, partial-VAT and Gift Aid capabilities
Native Salesforce and charity-CRM integration path
limitations: Supplier positions the charity product for organisations turning over £500,000 or more
Not a church-specific pastoral, membership, safeguarding or children’s system
Product DPA, sub-processors, exact hosting and migration or export commitments require a current written pack

procurementVerdict.problem: Producing controlled charity accounts and fund reports where existing finance and Salesforce charity data are fragmented
procurementVerdict.differentiator: A UK charity-accounting product built natively inside Salesforce with published SORP and Gift Aid capability
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Run a supplier demonstration using representative restricted-fund, Gift Aid, partial-VAT and year-end reporting scenarios; model all full-user, reviewer, implementation and Salesforce costs, then review the product DPA, international-transfer safeguards and complete finance-data export before commitment.
